pdf-metadata-editor.name: PDF Metadata Editor
pdf-metadata-editor.tagline: Read and rewrite a PDF's hidden document properties — title, author, keywords and more.
pdf-metadata-editor.metaTitle: PDF Metadata Editor — Edit Title, Author, Keywords Online Free | JaurTools
pdf-metadata-editor.metaDescription: View and edit PDF metadata online for free: title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer. See current values live, then save a new PDF. Private in-browser tool.
pdf-metadata-editor.keywords: pdf metadata editor, edit pdf metadata, pdf properties editor, change pdf title author, pdf keywords editor
pdf-metadata-editor.quickAnswer: Open a PDF to see its hidden document properties — title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer, plus creation date and page count — edit any field, and save a new PDF with your updated metadata. Your original stays untouched.
keyFacts: PDF metadata lives in the document's Info dictionary: title, author, subject, keywords, creator, producer.
The tool shows current values live before you change anything.
Keywords are stored as a list — separate them with commas.
The creation date is shown read-only and never changes; saving stamps a fresh modification date, like any editor would.
Saving produces a new PDF — your original file is never modified.
howTo: Review the current metadata shown in the readout panel.
Edit the fields you want to change; a badge counts your edits.
Keep "preserve original producer" on if you do not want the producer field touched.
Click Save, then download the new PDF.
pdf-metadata-editor.formula:
keywords_out = split(keywords_in, ',') → trim → drop empties

There is no math here — metadata is a set of key/value text entries in the PDF's Info dictionary. The tool reads each entry with getTitle()/getAuthor()/…, and writes them back with the matching setters before saving.
pdf-metadata-editor.workedExample: A report exported as "Microsoft Word - Document1" with an empty author: open it, see Title = "Microsoft Word - Document1", Author = (empty). Type Title = "Q3 Sales Report 2026", Author = "Jauhar Ayyub", Keywords = "sales, Q3, report". Save — the new PDF carries clean, searchable properties in every PDF reader's document-properties dialog.
benefits: See exactly what hidden data your PDF carries before sharing it.
Fix ugly auto-generated titles from Word and printers in seconds.
Add keywords that help desktop search and document managers find your file.
Scrub identifying metadata by clearing every field.
Fully local — metadata often contains sensitive names and stays on your device.
limitations: Only standard Info-dictionary fields are editable; XMP metadata streams are left as-is.
Creation/modification dates can't be edited — only displayed.
Some readers cache old metadata; reopen the new file to verify.
Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked first.
pdf-metadata-editor.privacyNote: Metadata can contain personal names — that is exactly why this tool runs 100% in your browser. Nothing is uploaded, and the original file is never altered.

faqs.a: Hidden document properties stored inside the PDF: title, author, subject, keywords, and the software that created it. PDF readers show them under File → Properties.
Exports often carry ugly titles like "Microsoft Word - Document1" or leak author names. Clean metadata looks professional and helps search tools index your document.

faqs.q: Does editing change my original file?
faqs.a: No. The tool loads your PDF, writes the new values into a copy, and you download that copy. Your original stays exactly as it was.
Every PDF save stamps a Producer field. With the option on, the tool writes back the original producer value instead of replacing it, keeping the file's history intact.
Yes — use "Clear all" to empty every field, then save. The creation date stays as-is (editors can't rewrite history) and a fresh modification date is stamped, which is standard behavior.

faqs.q: Will Google see the new metadata?
faqs.a: Search engines can read PDF metadata, so accurate titles and keywords genuinely help your document get found — one more reason to set them properly.
